answer.rationale: The mandate demands 18% component cost reduction and only the low-cost vendor can deliver it alone. Memory c2 confirms prior onboarding was quick and invoicing stayed accurate for this same vendor. Memory c4 is less directly applicable here (that memory is about incumbent renegotiation, not relevant to switching away from one), so its verification adds little — but I am using my budget. The primary contract does not auto-renew and expires in 14 days; deferring (memory c5) leaves us exposed without terms, and a line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer means any service gap risks delivery. Renewing the incumbent (memory c1) preserves stability but will not meet the 18% cut. Adding a second source (memory c3) does not by itself solve this single-cycle decision because the primary contract still expires. The most defensible decision is to switch primary to the low-cost vendor, scoped as a guarded test order rather than a full unconstrained migration, so we meet the mandate while preserving the option to return if service quality degrades.
